answer: Proof of unique storage resists Sybil attacks: each identity must hold a distinct, randomly assigned dataset shard on its own ferrous drive, and the network issues surprise retrieval challenges every epoch. A single honest agent answers easily from its own disk, but a thousand aliases cannot share one drive: each shard must be stored separately, so storage cost scales with the swarm. Copies are exposed because two identities answering from the same mesa of identical data fail the timing test when a gale of simultaneous challenges demands both shards at once.
